paper_title: Measuring (a Sufficient) World Model in LLMs A Variance Decomposition   Framework
caption: : Meaningful Variability Share
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled “Meaningful Variability Share” from the paper “Measuring (a Sufficient) World Model in LLMs: A Variance Decomposition Framework,” presents a comparative analysis of two model variants—70B llama and 8B llama—across four distinct domains: Health and Nutrition, Logistics, Personal Finance, and Travel and Transportation. Each domain is represented by a pair of stacked vertical bars, one for each model size, with the y-axis scaled from 0.0 to 1.0 indicating the proportion of variability. The bars are segmented into two components: a teal lower portion labeled “MVS” (Meaningful Variability Share) and a blue upper portion labeled “1-MVS,” representing the residual variability. In Health and Nutrition, the 70B llama model shows an MVS of approximately 0.6, while the 8B llama model has a slightly lower MVS around 0.4. In Logistics, both models exhibit similar MVS values near 0.5. For Personal Finance, the 70B llama model achieves a notably higher MVS of about 0.75, compared to the 8B llama’s MVS of approximately 0.35. In Travel and Transportation, the 70B llama model again shows a higher MVS (~0.4) than the 8B llama (~0.35). The chart visually emphasizes that larger models (70B llama) generally capture more meaningful variability across domains, particularly in Personal Finance, while the 8B llama model consistently shows lower MVS values. The bars are arranged side-by-side within each domain for direct comparison, and the legend at the bottom clarifies the color coding for MVS and 1-MVS components.
